solution:
Solution (a)** Since, the vectors \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are collinear.\
\(\therefore\) There exist scalar \(\lambda\) such that \(\begin{matrix}
 & \alpha = \lambda\beta \\
 \Rightarrow & (x - 2)\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b} = \lambda\{(3 + 2x)\mathbf{a} - 2\mathbf{b}\} \\
 \Rightarrow & (x - 2) - \lambda(3 + 2x)\mathbf{a} + (1 + 2\lambda)\mathbf{b} = 0 \\
 \Rightarrow & x - 2 - \lambda(3 + 2x) = 0\text{~and~}1 + 2\lambda = 0 \\
 \Rightarrow & x - 2 - \lambda(3 + 2x) = 0\text{~and~}\lambda = - \frac{1}{2} \\
 \Rightarrow & x - 2 + \frac{1}{2}(3 + 2x) = 0 \\
 \Rightarrow & 4x - 1 = 0 \\
 \Rightarrow & x = \frac{1}{4}
\end{matrix}\)

Thus, if \(\mathbf{a},\mathbf{b}\) are non-collinear vectors, but \(\alpha,\beta\) are collinear, then \(x = \frac{1}{4}\).
